procedures.title: Rear torque control arm: remove, repair and install
steps: (continued) ...so its flat matches the flat in the spindle support fork; fit the nut and torque to specification.
Fit the shock absorber lower eye and tighten its nut to specification.
Reconnect the spring end (Spring Installation steps 3-6).
If fitted, reconnect the stabilizer shaft to the torque arm (see Stabilizer Shaft Replacement).
Reconnect the brake line at the caliper and torque arm; bleed the brakes (see Section 5).
Refit the wheel and tire and lower the car; then torque the torque arm pivot bolt to specification.

procedures.title: Rear suspension crossmember: remove, repair and install
steps: Removal: disconnect and remove the spring (see Spring Removal).
Remove the differential carrier (see Differential Carrier Removal).
Support the crossmember, remove the bolts holding its isolation mounts to the frame and lower it (see figure 62 in the manual).
Remove the bolts holding the carrier cover to the crossmember.
Check the rubber isolation mounts for aging and replace as needed.
Mount repair: bend back the mount tabs so it can come out (see figure 63 in the manual).
Set the crossmember on a support and press the mount out with pipe or tubing of the right size on the outer shell or inner insert.
Place the new mount, squeeze the outer sleeve and press it in until fully and squarely seated.
Installation: bolt the carrier cover to the crossmember and torque to specification.
Lift the crossmember into place, fit the mounting bolts and torque to specification.
Install the differential carrier (see Differential Carrier Installation).
Install the spring and the wheels and tires, remove the frame supports and lower the car.
